extracted.intended_audience: educational institution administrators (Title IX coordinators), institutional legal counsel, advocates, OCR staff, and stakeholders participating in notice-and-comment on Title IX rules
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble discussion and responses to public comments on the Department's final Title IX regulations, addressing religious exemptions, elementary/secondary (ESE) vs postsecondary (PSE) differences, grievance procedures, and related procedural and transparency issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious exemption statutory scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX provides a religious exemption for educational institutions controlled by a religious organization under 20 U.S.C. 1681(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An institution is exempt only to the extent that application of Title IX would not be consistent with the religious tenets of the controlling organization. The Department cannot eliminate the statutory religious exemption by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden to assert religious exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The burden remains on the recipient (the institution) to establish and assert a religious exemption to Title IX, not on students or complainants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient must demonstrate that it is an educational institution controlled by a religious organization and that application of Title IX/its implementing regulations would conflict with its religious tenets.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to request assurance letter before invoking exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither Title IX nor the final regulations require a recipient to request an assurance of a religious exemption from OCR before asserting the exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR's assurance-letter process is optional; recipients may invoke an exemption without prior written submission to the Assistant Secretary. The Department declines to require or codify a mandatory assurance-letter policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR processing of complaints and religious exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR and the Department will process complaints in the normal course and will consider any asserted religious exemption as part of an investigation rather than automatically staying or ignoring the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department disagrees that invoking an exemption will put a complaint on hold. Complaints will be processed promptly and religious-exemption assertions will be evaluated during the investigation like other exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No automatic notification requirement to complainant of recipient's invocation of exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department does not, by rule, require OCR to notify complainants when a recipient invokes a religious exemption; OCR's current practices (including Case Processing Manual procedures) govern notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in the final regulations prevents a recipient from informing a complainant, and complainants can appeal Department determinations or direct inquiries to a recipient's Title IX Coordinator or the Assistant Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and assurance letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence between OCR and recipient institutions, including assurance letters, is subject to FOIA requirements and may be posted on OCR's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such publications are necessarily incomplete and not required; OCR often posts correspondence and documents are available via FOIA requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Against requiring publication/listing of recipients with exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require OCR to publish a list, book, or web page enumerating all recipients that have obtained religious-exemption assurance letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists would be incomplete and could mischaracterize scope of exemptions; Congress did not require such reporting under Title IX, and the Department will not impose additional burdens on recipients' constitutional rights to create such a list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of entanglement and scrutiny of theological tenets
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR generally avoids closely scrutinizing or questioning theological tenets or sincerely held religious beliefs of a recipient that invokes the religious exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assurance-letter application process is optional and does not create entanglement according to the Department; OCR seeks to avoid scrutinizing religious doctrine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious exemption cannot be used to avoid criminal punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Religious exemptions cannot realistically be invoked to avoid punishment for criminal activity; the Department does not punish criminal activity but enforces Title IX's non-discrimination mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent a specific factual example, asserting a religious exemption to avoid criminal liability is not viewed as acceptable under Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'controlled by a religious organization' deferred
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to define 'controlled by a religious organization' in this rulemaking and will address that definition in a subsequent notice of proposed rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical assistance will remain available; recipients and the public should not rely on a new regulatory definition from this final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESE actual-knowledge trigger expanded
rubrics_metrics.description: For elementary and secondary schools (ESE), 'actual knowledge' is defined more broadly to include notice to any ESE employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recognizes ESE staff and the special in loco parentis relationship; notice to any ESE employee triggers the recipient's duty to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: ESE not required to use live hearings or cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: ESE recipients are not required to conduct live hearings with cross-examination as part of their grievance processes under §106.45(b)(6)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an ESE recipient chooses to use a hearing model, it does not need to comply with the postsecondary-specific hearing provisions in §106.45(b)(6)(i). Recipients retain flexibility to make processes less formal or intimidating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures: prompt offering
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must promptly offer supportive measures to a complainant whenever an ESE employee has notice of sexual harassment or allegations of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures are designed to protect safety, deter harassment, and preserve equal educational access and must be offered without waiting for initiation of a formal grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures may impose some burdens but not unreasonably so
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures cannot 'unreasonably burden' the respondent, but they may impose some burdens (e.g., changing a respondent's class or activity schedule) if necessary to protect safety and equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have wide discretion to implement supportive measures appropriate to the ESE environment; measures should be balanced against respondents' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal authority for imminent threat
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may remove a respondent from education programs or activities on an emergency basis under §106.44(c) if the respondent presents an imminent threat to physical health or safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency removals are available consistent with the final regulations; they are a separate authority from discipline and may be used to protect safety pending resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of non-responsibility maintained
rubrics_metrics.description: The presumption that a respondent is not responsible must be preserved in Title IX grievance processes to avoid treating respondents as responsible absent resolution under §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presumption protects due process even while allowing flexibility to address safety and equal access before final resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures: required written findings and reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinations regarding responsibility must be accompanied by specific findings and a written report complying with §106.45 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although commenters argued this burdens ESE schools, the Department maintains requirements for written determinations; recipients may, however, adapt procedures within the regulations' framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility for ESE in grievance timing and formality
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may conduct grievance processes under timeframes the recipient has designated as reasonable for an ESE environment and may make the process less formal/intimidating while providing equal opportunity to parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations permit discretion to minimize resource expenditure and tailor procedures to the ESE context (e.g., limited or no live hearings, modified investigative steps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal resolution permitted but with caution
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations allow recipients discretion to facilitate informal resolution (e.g., mediation), but commenters raised concerns about trauma and appropriateness in ESE contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may use informal resolution where permissible, but must ensure parties' rights and avoid pressuring complainants; informal resolution can end an investigation if both parties voluntarily agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource and capacity considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may adjust procedures to minimize the resources expended on each allegation; the Department expects efficiencies over time as procedures become routine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While concerns exist about costs (e.g., separate investigator, evidence-sharing), the Department believes predictable rules will reduce confusion and potentially lower long-term costs; technical assistance is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and non-discrimination posting requirements (§106.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.8 requires recipients to notify applicants, students, parents/guardians, employees, and relevant unions or organizations of the recipient's notice of non-discrimination on the basis of sex and its grievance procedures and how to report or file complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must provide adequate notice of non-discrimination and grievance processes; §106.8(b)(2)(ii) also prohibits using publications that state the recipient treats applicants/students/employees differently on the basis of sex except as allowed by Title IX or the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to inquire and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may inquire about the application of Title IX to a particular recipient by contacting the recipient's Title IX Coordinator, the Assistant Secretary, or both; complainants have appeal rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainants may raise concerns about invocation of religious exemptions on appeal and may direct inquiries to specified officials per §106.8(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Department technical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department and OCR will provide technical assistance to recipients seeking answers about specific factual circumstances involving the final regulations or religious exemptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical assistance is available rather than attempting to resolve complex fact-specific questions within the rulemaking preamble.
